detail.body:
## Purpose

Adds a generation health check at `/health_generate`

The implementation is based on PR #59179, with improvements that cover more edge cases with DP > 1 and report why the server is not ready. I've added the author of #59179 as a committer on this PR. Please see #59179 for context on the initial design.

This does not duplicate other work: it continues #59179, and I'm not aware of another open PR adding a generation health check.

### Background

For long running inference deployments for online serving as well as RL use-cases, there can be a variety of inference engine failures or hangs. Broadly there are two sources of failures / hangs:

1. Infrastructure failures: GPU failures, network failures, etc. Some of these are recoverable (transient error that succeeds on retry) while some are not (GPU failure).
2. Software bugs: There are two styles of errors here:
a. Probabilistic, recoverable: Errors that happen due to low-probability events such as:
      1. An illegal memory access with vLLM that occurs once in millions of generations.
      2. A collective hang during weight syncing in DPEP setups.
      3. Generation [hang](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44185) with spec decoding + MoE + DP.
b. Irrecoverable bugs: Bugs that are deterministic failures in certain state.
      1. Misconfigurations, unsupported kernel on certain hardware, etc.

A generation health check helps users detect and recover from failures of class 1. and 2.a.

<details>
<summary> List of failures to handle</summary>

Here are a few relevant issues for vLLM server failures / hangs:

| Issue | Brief description | Failure mode |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| #44185 | DP + EP + MTP/speculative decoding can hang near `max_model_len` when DP ranks disagree about whether the drafter path should run. | EngineCore forward/collective hang; processes may stay alive while affected requests stop making progress. |
| #43547 | MoE + DP can drift collective sequence after zero-token scheduled steps skip DP coordination, eventually hanging a real MoE collective. | EngineCore forward collective hang, likely with worker processes alive but blocked in `reduce_scatter` or a related collective. |
| #36594 / #51481 | DPEP pause/wake coordination can leave DP ranks or the coordinator in the wrong running state around `pause_generation`, `sleep()`, `collective_rpc`, or online weight update. The older issue covers a late `START_DP_WAVE` re-arming a paused engine; the later PR fixes the coordinator assuming engines started merely because it forwarded a wake. | DP wave/coordinator control-plane hang: processes can stay alive, but drain times out, frontends may stop sending `FIRST_REQ`, or ranks can enter mismatched collectives during weight-sync/control RPCs. |
| #53130 | Running chunked-prefill work can consume the scheduler token budget every step, so waiting/deferred requests are not admitted or promoted. | Admission starvation / request-level timeout, not a full EngineCore hang; existing running requests may still progress. |
| #54173 | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next prefix-caching/GDN path can hit CUBLAS internal error or illegal memory access in fused Mamba/GDN kernels. | Kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure after the async CUDA error surfaces. |
| #37035 | MTP/hybrid GDN illegal memory access under load, later tied to a drafter block-size/cache-pressure bug. | Kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure; may require long-running/load-heavy traffic to trigger. |
| #60109 | HiSparse + GLM TP8 on B200 hits illegal memory access when a new request wave is admitted after a previous wave completes. | Wave-transition kernel crash leading to EngineCore or worker failure. |
| #59768 | SimpleCPUOffloadConnector can hit illegal memory access while async CPU-to-GPU prefix load is in flight. | Connector/load-side CUDA race causing EngineCore or worker failure, especially on prefix-cache/offload paths. |
| #45388 | KV-offloading plus prefix caching can deadlock the V1 scheduler under KV-cache pressure: the engine reaches `running=0`, `scheduled=0`, waiting requests remain stuck, and throughput stays at zero. | Scheduler/request-progress hang with EngineCore process alive. |

</details>

### What kind of health checks will detect such failures / hangs?

| Health check | Description | Failures caught |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Existing `/health` endpoint | API server and Engine process liveness. | #54173, #37035, #60109, #59768, once the CUDA/kernel failure surfaces as EngineCore or worker death. |
| `/health_generate` in SGLang | Gets the scheduler to admit a dummy request. If the scheduler is busy (running + waiting > 0), return early with a success response. If the scheduler is idle, execute a dummy forward pass (single token). | #44185, #43547, #36594 / #51481, #54173, #37035, #60109, #59768. However, issues like #45388 are not caught - this is because the scheduler can seem busy (running + waiting > 0) when it's not making any progress (running = 0, waiting > 0) for a long time. |
| Proposed `/health_generate` in vLLM (SGLang's check plus busy-stall detection) | Evaluated per engine rank. If a rank is busy, check how long it has been since it last processed tokens; past a timeout, the server is not ready. If a rank is idle, run a dummy forward pass on it and wait for it to finish on the device. If a rank is sleeping, report it. | #44185, #43547, #36594 / #51481, #54173, #37035, #60109, #59768 and #45388. |

One failure that is not caught by any of the methods above is #53130. I would argue that it is out of scope for the current effort, since the issue is a bit unclear on the exact root cause for the bug. A part of the issue also mentions that the hang occurs when the scheduler is already busy and is able to make progress on running prefill inputs, which means that the engine is alive and healthy.

Note that we haven't discussed any recoverable errors from infrastructure failures. Typical failures here lead to collective timeouts or EngineCore process death, which are of a similar nature to the failures above.

### Changes on top of #59179

**Readiness evaluation**

- **Per rank.** Each engine rank is checked separately:
  - a sleeping rank reports `sleeping`;
  - a busy rank is checked for stalls;
  - an idle rank gets the GPU probe.

  So a busy DP rank no longer hides an idle rank that is stuck in a control RPC.
- **Progress comes only from the engines.** The frontend no longer marks a rank busy when it sends a request. That mark could leave the server reporting `stalled` while idle, if the engine dropped the request before scheduling it.
- **Connector cleanup is not a stall.** Steps that only drain KV-transfer cleanup for finished requests (e.g. a P/D prefill node waiting on a remote pull) count as progress.
- **A dedicated broadcast.** EngineCore publishes readiness to every API server in its own message. Nothing is attached to request outputs any more.

**The idle GPU probe**

- **New `check_health_gpu` on the worker:**
  - It runs the dummy forward pass without adding dummy LoRA adapters or removing loaded ones.
  - It waits for the device to finish before replying, so a fault or hang in the probe's own forward pass fails that same call.
- **Every TP and PP worker must reply.** PP stages don't communicate during a dummy run, so a fault on an earlier stage would otherwise go unnoticed.
- **Out-of-tree platforms:** `WorkerBase.check_health_gpu` raises `NotImplementedError`, so platforms that don't implement it report `probe_failed`.
- **Shared result:**
  - Concurrent callers share one in-flight probe per rank.
  - A successful probe is cached for `VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S`.

**DP > 1**

- Only count a DP dummy batch as progress when the rank has no local unfinished requests. A rank that holds requests but schedules nothing (e.g. #45388) keeps the wave alive with dummy batches, and was previously reported as making progress.
- Run the idle probe for DP > 1 instead of skipping it.
  - Dense DP ranks are independent engines and run the probe as with DP = 1.
  - MoE DP engines answer with a liveness-only ping, because a dummy batch outside the wave loop could deadlock against peer collectives. A busy loop stuck in a control RPC now makes the probe time out.

**Not-ready details**

- Every not-ready response is a 503 with a JSON body:
  ```json
  {"status": "not_ready", "reason": ..., "message": ..., <details>, "in_progress": [...]}
  ```
  - `reason` is one of `engine_dead`, `sleeping`, `stalled`, `probe_timeout` or `probe_failed`.
  - `engine_dead` returns only `status` and `reason`.
- `in_progress` lists the utility call each EngineCore is running, with its rank and elapsed time. EngineCore publishes the operation before running a utility and clears it afterwards, so every API server reports it, whichever one issued the call.

**Configuration**

| Env var | Default | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT` | 20 s | How long a caller waits for the idle probe before reporting `probe_timeout`. |
| `VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S` | 60 s | A busy rank with no progress for this long reports `stalled`. `0` disables the check. |
| `VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S` | 10 s | How long a successful idle probe is reused. `0` disables the cache. |

**Scope**

- **Rust frontend:**
  - The Rust client decodes the new readiness messages and ignores them, so normal Rust serving is unaffected.
  - The Rust `/health_generate` endpoint, and aggregating it in the DP supervisor, will come in a follow-up PR.
- **DP supervisor:** its `/ready` and `/readyz` are unchanged.
- **Render-only servers** (no engine) return 200.

**Why report additional not-ready details?**

Downstream applications, such as a load balancer or a health monitor daemon, decide whether to tear down a server based on the response. A 503 from `/health_generate` does not mean the server is broken; it means the server can't serve generation requests right now. For example, it returns 503 while waiting for a weight sync to complete.

### Comparison with the `/fault_tolerance/` APIs

The current fault tolerance APIs can detect failures/hangs during the forward pass in DPEP MoE deployments. This PR targets a broader set of failures/hangs, which is why it adds a separate `/health_generate` endpoint.

### Known limitations

- **Probe stuck for a long time, then recovers.** If the idle probe is stuck for longer than `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (300 s) and then completes, its late reply stays queued. The next executor RPC reads it, and the engine fails. The same applies to any timed-out `collective_rpc` utility call today.
- **`VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT <= 0`** makes every idle probe report `probe_timeout`.
- **Rust frontend:** `/health_generate` is not served yet (see Scope above).

## Test Plan

Apart from the unit tests added in #59179, I've added real E2E tests that cover failure modes from the list above. I think these E2E tests are important to guarantee failure recovery at the engine level.

New tests:

- **Unit tests** for:
  - per-rank evaluation, the DP probe and connector-cleanup progress;
  - shared and timed-out probes;
  - reason and `in_progress` reporting;
  - the engine-side operation broadcast.
- **Fault-injection E2E tests** in `tests/v1/engine/readiness`, using `--scheduler-cls` and `--worker-extension-cls`, split by GPU count:
  - `test_ready_single_gpu.py` (1 GPU): scheduler stall, a latent CUDA fault while idle (including a fault in the probe's own forward pass), and no false positives.
  - `test_ready_multi_gpu.py` (2 GPUs): MoE and dense DP = 2 variants, including a rank stuck in a mismatched DP collective, and a PP = 2 CUDA fault on the stage that doesn't return outputs.
  - These run in the V1 Engine and Distributed CI steps.
- **Rust:** a check that a Python-encoded readiness message decodes in the Rust client.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm_health.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_basic.py -v
pytest tests/v1/engine/readiness/test_ready_single_gpu.py -v   # 1 GPU
pytest tests/v1/engine/readiness/test_ready_multi_gpu.py -v    # 2 GPUs
cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client
```

## Test Result

| Suite | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| `tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm_health.py` | 26/26 passed |
| `tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_basic.py` | 9/9 passed (`server_load` deselected, as in CI) |

| `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_dp_supervisor.py` | passed (unchanged from main) |
| Rust `vllm-engine-core-client` | 133/133 passed |

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Runtime fault injection for `/health_generate` end-to-end tests.
+
+Loaded into the server via ``--scheduler-cls`` / ``--worker-extension-cls``.
+Scheduler faults are toggled with flag files under ``$VLLM_READY_FAULT_DIR``
+(the scheduler lives in the EngineCore process). Worker faults are triggered
+through the dev ``/collective_rpc`` endpoint, which only forwards strings.
+"""
+
+import os
+import time
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.async_scheduler import AsyncScheduler
+
+FAULT_DIR_ENV = "VLLM_READY_FAULT_DIR"
+SCHEDULER_STALL = "scheduler_stall"
+UTILITY_HANG = "utility_hang"
+
+
+def _launch_illegal_memory_access() -> None:
+    import triton
+    import triton.language as tl
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _oob_store(ptr, offset):
+        tl.store(ptr + offset, 1.0)
+
+    buf = torch.empty(1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    _oob_store[(1,)](buf, 1 << 42)
+
+
+class FaultInjectionScheduler(AsyncScheduler):
+    """While the ``scheduler_stall`` flag exists, schedule zero tokens.
+
+    Mimics #45388: requests stay waiting but no tokens are ever scheduled,
+    while the EngineCore busy loop keeps spinning.
+    """
+
+    max_num_scheduled_tokens: int
+
+    def schedule(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        fault_dir = os.environ.get(FAULT_DIR_ENV)
+        if fault_dir is None or not os.path.exists(
+            os.path.join(fault_dir, SCHEDULER_STALL)
+        ):
+            return super().schedule(*args, **kwargs)
+        saved = self.max_num_scheduled_tokens
+        self.max_num_scheduled_tokens = 0
+        try:
+            return super().schedule(*args, **kwargs)
+        finally:
+            self.max_num_scheduled_tokens = saved
+
+
+class FaultInjectionWorkerExtension:
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig
+    model_runner: Any
+    rank: int
+
+    def _fault_targets_me(self, dp_ranks: str) -> bool:
+        # Dense DP engines keep data_parallel_rank=0; the index is the DP rank.
+        rank = self.vllm_config.parallel_config.data_parallel_index
+        return rank in {int(r) for r in dp_ranks.split(",")}
+
+    def fault_hang_while_flag_set(self, flag: str) -> None:
+        """Block this control call while the flag exists, like a weight
+        sync stuck waiting on its peers."""
+        path = os.path.join(os.environ[FAULT_DIR_ENV], flag)
+        while os.path.exists(path):
+            time.sleep(0.1)
+
+    def fault_ima_now(self, dp_ranks: str) -> None:
+        """Launch an illegal memory access without synchronizing.
+
+        Models a latent async CUDA fault that has not surfaced yet because
+        nothing synchronized afterwards.
+        """
+        if not self._fault_targets_me(dp_ranks):
+            return
+        _launch_illegal_memory_access()
+
+    def fault_ima_now_on_worker(self, worker_rank: str) -> None:
+        """Like ``fault_ima_now``, on one TP/PP worker of the engine."""
+        if self.rank == int(worker_rank):
+            _launch_illegal_memory_access()
+
+    def fault_ima_on_next_forward(self, dp_ranks: str) -> None:
+        """Launch an illegal memory access at the end of the next forward
+        pass, so the fault belongs to the readiness probe's own GPU work."""
+        if not self._fault_targets_me(dp_ranks):
+            return
+
+        def hook(*_):
+            handle.remove()
+            _launch_illegal_memory_access()
+
+        handle = self.model_runner.get_model().register_forward_hook(hook)
+
+    def fault_dp_mismatched_collective(self, dp_ranks: str) -> None:
+        """Enter a DP all-reduce that the other ranks never join (#36594)."""
+        if not self._fault_targets_me(dp_ranks):
+            return
+        from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_dp_group
+
+        t = torch.ones(1, device="cuda")
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(t, group=get_dp_group().device_group)
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""`/health_generate` against injected failures across two GPUs (DP=2 and PP=2).
+
+MoE DP ranks step in lockstep waves where idle ranks run dummy batches, and
+must not be probed with an ad-hoc dummy batch; dense DP ranks are independent
+engines that can be probed like a single engine.
+"""
+
+import time
+
+import pytest
+
+from tests.utils import multi_gpu_marks
+
+from .fault_injection import SCHEDULER_STALL
+from .utils import STALL_TIMEOUT_S, ready_probe_server
+
+pytestmark = multi_gpu_marks(num_gpus=2)
+
+MOE_MODEL = "ibm-research/PowerMoE-3b"
+DENSE_MODEL = "hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM"
+MOE_DP_ARGS = [
+    "--data-parallel-size",
+    "2",
+    "--enable-expert-parallel",
+    # Weights are dummy; two layers keep startup and memory small.
+    "--hf-overrides",
+    '{"num_hidden_layers": 2}',
+]
+DENSE_DP_ARGS = ["--data-parallel-size", "2"]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def moe_server(tmp_path_factory):
+    with ready_probe_server(
+        MOE_MODEL, MOE_DP_ARGS, tmp_path_factory.mktemp("faults")
+    ) as srv:
+        yield srv
+
+
+def test_moe_no_false_positive(moe_server):
+    """An idle rank inside a wave keeps counting as progressing, and probes
+    racing with wave starts do not flap."""
+    with moe_server.busy(dp_ranks=(0,)):
+        assert moe_server.stays_ready(STALL_TIMEOUT_S + 3)
+    for i in range(10):
+        moe_server.generate_in_background(8, dp_rank=i % 2)
+        assert moe_server.status() == 200
+        time.sleep(0.2 * (i % 3))
+
+
+def test_moe_scheduler_stall(moe_server):
+    """#45388 under DP: ranks hold requests but schedule nothing while the
+    wave keeps running dummy batches."""
+    moe_server.set_fault(SCHEDULER_STALL)
+    try:
+        moe_server.generate_in_background(8, dp_rank=0)
+        moe_server.generate_in_background(8, dp_rank=1)
+        assert moe_server.wait_until_unready() is not None
+        assert moe_server.status("/health") == 200
+    finally:
+        moe_server.clear_fault(SCHEDULER_STALL)
+    assert moe_server.wait_until_ready()
+
+
+def test_moe_collective_mismatch_while_idle(tmp_path):
+    """#36594 class: rank 0 is wedged in a DP collective inside a control RPC
+    while there is no traffic."""
+    with ready_probe_server(MOE_MODEL, MOE_DP_ARGS, tmp_path) as srv:
+        assert srv.status() == 200
+        srv.rpc("fault_dp_mismatched_collective", "0", background=True)
+        assert srv.wait_until_unready() is not None
+        assert srv.status("/health") == 200
+        # Any API server can name the wedged operation and rank.
+        for _ in range(4):
+            body = srv.ready_body()
+            assert body["reason"] == "probe_timeout"
+            stuck = {(op["operation"], op["engine_rank"]) for op in body["in_progress"]}
+            assert ("collective_rpc:fault_dp_mismatched_collective", 0) in stuck
+
+
+def test_dense_latent_cuda_error_while_idle(tmp_path):
+    """A latent CUDA fault on an idle dense DP rank is caught by its probe."""
+    with ready_probe_server(DENSE_MODEL, DENSE_DP_ARGS, tmp_path) as srv:
+        assert srv.status() == 200
+        srv.rpc("fault_ima_now", "1")
+        assert srv.wait_until_unready() is not None
+
+
+def test_cuda_error_on_non_output_pp_stage(tmp_path):
+    """The probe checks every worker, not only the last PP stage that returns
+    model outputs; PP dummy runs do not communicate across stages."""
+    args = ["--pipeline-parallel-size", "2"]
+    with ready_probe_server(DENSE_MODEL, args, tmp_path) as srv:
+        assert srv.status() == 200
+        srv.rpc("fault_ima_now_on_worker", "0")
+        assert srv.status() == 503

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project

+import os
+import threading
+import time
+from contextlib import contextmanager, suppress
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import requests
+
+from tests.utils import RemoteOpenAIServer
+
+from .fault_injection import FAULT_DIR_ENV
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
+
+STALL_TIMEOUT_S = 5.0
+PROBE_TIMEOUT_S = 5.0
+DETECT_DEADLINE_S = STALL_TIMEOUT_S + PROBE_TIMEOUT_S + 15.0
+
+
+class ReadyProbeServer:
+    """A vLLM server with fault injection hooks and readiness helpers."""
+
+    def __init__(self, server: RemoteOpenAIServer, model: str, fault_dir: Path):
+        self.server = server
+        self.model = model
+        self.fault_dir = fault_dir
+
+    def status(self, path: str = "/health_generate") -> int | None:
+        """Return the HTTP status, or None if the server is unreachable."""
+        try:
+            return requests.get(
+                self.server.url_for(path.lstrip("/")), timeout=30
+            ).status_code
+        except requests.RequestException:
+            return None
+
+    def ready_body(self) -> dict:
+        resp = requests.get(self.server.url_for("health_generate"), timeout=30)
+        return resp.json() if resp.status_code != 200 else {}
+
+    def wait_until_unready(self) -> float | None:
+        """Return seconds until ``/health_generate`` stops returning 200, or None."""
+        start = time.monotonic()
+        while time.monotonic() - start < DETECT_DEADLINE_S:
+            if self.status() != 200:
+                return time.monotonic() - start
+            time.sleep(0.5)
+        return None
+
+    def wait_until_ready(self) -> bool:
+        start = time.monotonic()
+        while time.monotonic() - start < DETECT_DEADLINE_S:
+            if self.status() == 200:
+                return True
+            time.sleep(0.5)
+        return False
+
+    def stays_ready(self, duration_s: float) -> bool:
+        start = time.monotonic()
+        while time.monotonic() - start < duration_s:
+            if self.status() != 200:
+                return False
+            time.sleep(0.5)
+        return True
+
+    def generate(self, max_tokens: int = 8, dp_rank: int | None = None) -> int:
+        headers = {} if dp_rank is None else {"X-data-parallel-rank": str(dp_rank)}
+        resp = requests.post(
+            self.server.url_for("v1/completions"),
+            json={
+                "model": self.model,
+                "prompt": "Hello",
+                "max_tokens": max_tokens,
+                "ignore_eos": True,
+            },
+            headers=headers,
+            timeout=600,
+        )
+        return resp.status_code
+
+    def generate_in_background(self, max_tokens: int, dp_rank: int | None = None):
+        threading.Thread(
+            target=self._generate_quietly, args=(max_tokens, dp_rank), daemon=True
+        ).start()
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def busy(self, dp_ranks: tuple[int | None, ...] = (None,)):
+        """Keep the given DP ranks continuously busy with requests."""
+        stop = threading.Event()
+
+        def loop(dp_rank):
+            while not stop.is_set():
+                self._generate_quietly(64, dp_rank)
+
+        threads = [
+            threading.Thread(target=loop, args=(rank,), daemon=True)
+            for rank in dp_ranks
+            for _ in range(4)
+        ]
+        for t in threads:
+            t.start()
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            stop.set()
+            for t in threads:
+                t.join(timeout=60)
+
+    def _generate_quietly(self, max_tokens: int, dp_rank: int | None) -> None:
+        with suppress(requests.RequestException):
+            self.generate(max_tokens, dp_rank)
+
+    def rpc(self, method: str, *args: str, background: bool = False) -> None:
+        """Call a worker method through the dev ``/collective_rpc`` endpoint."""
+
+        def call():
+            with suppress(requests.RequestException):
+                requests.post(
+                    self.server.url_for("collective_rpc"),
+                    json={"method": method, "args": list(args)},
+                    timeout=600,
+                )
+
+        if background:
+            threading.Thread(target=call, daemon=True).start()
+        else:
+            call()
+
+    def set_fault(self, name: str) -> None:
+        (self.fault_dir / name).touch()
+
+    def clear_fault(self, name: str) -> None:
+        (self.fault_dir / name).unlink(missing_ok=True)
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def ready_probe_server(model: str, extra_args: list[str], fault_dir: Path):
+    fault_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    env = {
+        "VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE": "1",
+        "VLLM_READY_STALL_TIMEOUT_S": str(STALL_TIMEOUT_S),
+        "VLLM_HEALTH_CHECK_GPU_TIMEOUT": str(PROBE_TIMEOUT_S),
+        "VLLM_READY_IDLE_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_S": "0",
+        FAULT_DIR_ENV: str(fault_dir),
+        # The engine processes import the fault injection classes by name.
+        "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join(
+            p for p in (str(REPO_ROOT), os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH")) if p
+        ),
+    }
+    args = [
+        "--enforce-eager",
+        "--load-format",
+        "dummy",
+        "--max-model-len",
+        "512",
+        "--max-num-seqs",
+        "16",
+        "--max-num-batched-tokens",
+        "512",
+        "--kernel-config",
+        '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}',

+        "--gpu-memory-utilization",
+        "0.2",
+        "--scheduler-cls",
+        "tests.v1.engine.readiness.fault_injection.FaultInjectionScheduler",
+        "--worker-extension-cls",
+        "tests.v1.engine.readiness.fault_injection.FaultInjectionWorkerExtension",
+        *extra_args,
+    ]
+    with RemoteOpenAIServer(model, args, env_dict=env) as server:
+        yield ReadyProbeServer(server, model, fault_dir)

[P1] Update the Rust output protocol before broadcasting readiness messages

These fields produce readiness envelopes with 11 array elements, while rust/src/engine-core-client/src/protocol/output.rs still defines an eight-field WireEngineCoreOutputs using Deserialize_tuple. A real Python readiness frame passed to the same tuple decoder shape returns LengthMismatch(8). Even after accepting the additional fields, TryFrom<WireEngineCoreOutputs> rejects a readiness-only envelope as "invalid wire shape" because it has no request, utility, or wave payload.

The Rust transport forwards this decode error to the dispatcher, whose error path closes all request and utility registries. This affects ordinary Rust serving: IDLE-to-BUSY transitions and normal utility calls publish these messages even when nobody calls /ready.

Update both the Rust wire schema and readiness-only message handling, or negotiate/filter these notifications for unsupported consumers. Add a cross-language regression using an actual Python-encoded frame and verify that the Rust client continues serving after it.

Scheduler.has_requests() also remains true for finished requests awaiting delayed KV cleanup and connector/EC pending push work. If all live requests have finished, such a rank can keep stepping with zero scheduled tokens; _ready_progress_seq never advances, but this method continues to publish BUSY. This mark has no undo path, so `/ready` can stay at `stalled` on an idle, healthy server.

Since Rust `/ready` is planned as a follow-up anyway, the simplest fix is to leave both out of this PR: keep the supervisor's `/ready` as it was, and drop `test_check_ready`, which the readiness e2e tests already cover. Supervisor aggregation can come with the Rust endpoint.

Context: while evaluating this design I prototyped a much smaller opt-in variant, and I'm deliberately **not** opening a competing PR (repo policy on duplicate work) — posting it here in case any of it is useful for this PR.

Branch: https://github.com/dunjin/vllm/tree/feat/health-generate-probe
Diff vs `main`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/compare/main...dunjin:vllm:feat/health-generate-probe (~600 LOC incl. tests, 9 files)

Approach:
- `GET /health_generate` and `GET /health?generate=true` share one handler; plain `/health` stays cheap liveness, generation is opt-in, so existing k8s/sidecar probes never trigger GPU work.
- The probe sends one real request through `AsyncLLM.generate` (`max_tokens=1, min_tokens=1, temperature=0, ignore_eos=True`) and reports ready only after a token is produced. The timeout cancels the generator, which reuses `generate()`'s existing abort path, so no request is leaked.
- 503 body carries `{status, reason, message, request_id}` with `reason` ∈ `generation_timeout` / `no_token_generated` / `generation_failed` / `engine_dead` / `probe_error`; budget is `VLLM_HEALTH_GENERATE_TIMEOUT_S` (30s) or `?timeout=`.
- No EngineCore protocol or Rust wire changes. Role-agnostic for P/D: the prompt is 1 token, so an instance proves itself with a local prefill + one decode step without waiting for its peer.

Known trade-off, same as the #24491 discussion: the probe enqueues a request, so a deep queue can produce a false 503 — that's exactly why it is opt-in and separate from `/health`. Not covered: DP rank fan-out, and busy-but-stalled detection (which this PR's dummy-batch/progress path handles better).

Happy to fold any part into this PR, or drop it entirely — your call.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Review of `738c565e9b`, combining the current Codex model, Claude Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3, with follow-up cross-checking and focused probes. I recommend addressing the four correctness issues below before merging. The missing post-forward GPU completion wait is a separate code-established probe semantics gap; it was not reproduced with a GPU hang. Optional simplifications are labeled separately, and targeted regression tests are included with the relevant findings.

Validation: 23 readiness unit tests passed. CPU probes reproduced the mixed BUSY/IDLE DP false success and connector-cleanup false stall. A probe executing the actual LoRA setup context with simulated adapter storage demonstrated removal of preloaded adapters. A real Python readiness frame fed to a minimal Rust decoder using the existing eight-field serde_tuple shape returned LengthMismatch(8); the subsequent Rust dispatcher failure was traced in source, not exercised in a full frontend deployment. HTTP tests were blocked during collection by missing CUDA flash-attention extensions. No GPU fault-injection E2E or full Rust frontend suite was rerun.

Non-blocking: the tests could be shorter without losing coverage, e.g. a shared `EngineCoreProc` setup in `test_async_llm_health.py`, one parametrized test for the busy/sleeping/DP-wave cases that skip the dummy batch, and the three mocked `/ready` handler tests in `test_basic.py` merged into one parametrized test that still checks `reason` and the JSON body.
